findings.text: the section names a second and third change ("a gate log's terminal status may be named by the project's flight (an exit-line pattern) rather than only `EXIT=`", "a pre-existing failure declared on the run can be cited as such in a passed gate") with no assertion in the done-when and an explicit opt-out ("if left out, the reason is recorded here"), so the node's one verdict covers either one behaviour or three depending on what the worker chose, and its gate proves none of the optional two; `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:1781 already drops an entry naming a pre-existing failure`, so the second of these is a real behaviour change smuggled in as an aside

findings.reason: a worker told to accept a brief-named waiver either invents a brief-parsing mechanism the plan gives no evidence for or ships half the stated acceptance condition with no test that fails when it is absent.
findings.text: the Deliverable widens the waiver source to "whether it was recorded at completion or named in its brief", but the only suite-delta waiver in the tree is the one `crew complete --waive-suite-delta` writes onto the run record (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:344,425`, `reckon/crew/promotion.py:967,1391`) and nothing reads a waiver out of a brief, while the done-when's cases (a)–(d) exercise only the completion-recorded waiver — so the brief-named half is either an unbuildable condition or an unmeasured one
